_comment_key_facts: key_facts = the load-bearing factual claims a position rests on, each paired with the EXTERNAL source it came from. Added 2026-08-11 after a prior revision inverted the direction of a source's anchor move and then survived TWO re-verifications, because each re-verification re-read my own note and reproduced the error. A re-verification that does not diff the recorded claim against the source's actual words is confirmation, not verification. The audit rotation surfaces these for source-diffing. TAGGING CAVEAT (2026-08-12): the audit tags a source UNVERIFIED when it does not start with http, but a URL that 403s (congress.gov) is no more agent-verifiable than a prose 'sweep'. Where that happens, say so INLINE in the claim and name the independent falsifier used instead — do not let an unfetchable URL launder a claim into looking checked. SOURCE_DATE (2026-08-12): distinct from `checked`. `checked` is when I last LOOKED; `source_date` is when the source was PUBLISHED. The MacBook staleness cost 18pp precisely because those diverged invisibly — checked=1d ago on a source published 114d earlier, in a story that had moved three times since. For live-state sources (a leaderboard, an order book, a market description) the two are equal by construction. ATOMICITY REQUIRED (2026-08-13): one independently checkable assertion per entry, each with its own source and source_date. Bundled entries are how an unchecked fact hides inside a checked one — SpaceX's 'No plausible 2026 rival: OpenAI pushed to 2027, and a >$2.1T close would need an S-1 already public' bundled OpenAI's TIMING (checked twice) with every other rival's SIZE (never checked), and the second cost the project its largest prior correction. If an entry contains ' and ' joining two verifiable claims, split it.
